thread:
alex_support: Customer reporting a 401 invalid_api_key from our API when called from a GitHub Actions workflow after a recent key rotation. They pasted the workflow snippet and the secret value looks like it's PGP-armored (starts with -----BEGIN PGP MESSAGE-----). Anyone seen this?

jordan_customer: yeah that was me — I thought I uploaded the new key as a repo secret via the web UI but somehow I ended up pasting a .gpg file contents. The workflow injects ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY }} and the header is being sent. Response is 401.

maya_eng: ok — that would definitely fail. Our API expects a raw ascii key token, not an armored block. Can you confirm what the secret value looks like inside the runner? (don't post real key here, just show the first/last 8 chars or the header lines)

jordan_customer: here's an excerpt i can share, masked by GH: ``-----BEGIN PGP MESSAGE-----\n\nhQEMA6...restmasked...k2pL\n-----END PGP MESSAGE-----``

alex_support: thanks. quick checklist: 1) confirm the secret in Settings > Secrets is the raw token (no headers/footers), 2) run a quick check in the job before the call to print a safe fingerprint (length/hash) so we can see if it's the right format, 3) if wrong, rotate the token & update secret.

jordan_customer: how do i check inside the runner without exposing the token?

maya_eng: in the job you can print a hash or length check. e.g.:
```
- name: check secret fingerprint
  run: |
    echo "$REDWOOD_API_KEY" | wc -c  # prints length
    echo "$REDWOOD_API_KEY" | head -c 10 | sed -e 's/./*/g'  # show masked preview
```
That avoids printing the whole secret. For a raw Redwood key length is ~40-60 chars (alnum), not multi-line armor.

ci-bot: deployment/workflow (build) started by @jordan_customer :github:

jordan_customer: ran the check, it prints 1024 and the preview shows -----BEGIN. so it's definitely an armored file.

ops_lead: action items: 1) create a new API key in the console and copy the token string (do NOT upload the .gpg file). 2) update repo secret REDWOOD_API_KEY with the raw token (no newlines). 3) re-run workflow. If you need a short rotation window, we can create a temp key and revoke old.

alex_support: also added a note to docs to call out common GH Actions mistake: uploading entire file contents instead of the raw token. Leaving a quick repro here for support docs: create a test secret with file contents (e.g., cat mykey.gpg | gh secret set REDWOOD_API_KEY -b -) then call our API — you'll get 401 invalid_api_key and logs show header lines.

maya_eng: if they rotated already and still see 401 after replacing secret, we should check for trailing whitespace/newline. Recommend the user set the secret with `echo -n $TOKEN | gh secret set REDWOOD_API_KEY -b -` to avoid trailing newline.

jordan_customer: fixed by creating a new key and pasting raw token. workflow now succeeds. thanks! :rocket:

alex_support: great — closing the thread once customer confirms no further errors. :white_check_mark:
